episode_title: 125. Healthcare Energy Use – A Value Stream Worth Managing

real_qa.q: What percentage of energy waste exists in most health systems according to Eneration's findings?
real_qa.r: There is roughly 30% to 50% waste in most health systems—their energy 30% to 50% is wasted, representing a huge opportunity to address waste that goes directly to the bottom line and helps make financials better.

real_qa.q: How much did Gunderson Health System reduce energy consumption in 18 months using Kaizen events?
real_qa.r: Gunderson Health System achieved 20 percent energy efficiency improvement in about 18 months after conducting a Kaizen event to identify energy conservation opportunities, which spawned the Envision program.
real_qa.requete: Gunderson Health System energy efficiency 20 percent

real_qa.q: What percentage of U.S. greenhouse gas emissions are attributed to healthcare facilities?
real_qa.r: About 8% to 10% of greenhouse gas emissions in the U.S. are generated to serve healthcare facilities, and healthcare happens to be one of the biggest polluters in the country, particularly due to high requirements for filtration and ventilation in critical spaces.
real_qa.requete: healthcare greenhouse gas emissions percentage US

real_qa.q: What are the most effective low-cost methods to identify and eliminate energy waste in hospitals?
real_qa.r: The most effective low-cost methods include walking through buildings after hours to use the look, listen, and feel approach—identifying systems running when they shouldn't be, listening for fans and compressors running unnecessarily, and feeling for wasted heat. Additional measures include turning off lights in unoccupied spaces, optimizing pump motors and fan motors, and using building automation systems with variable frequency drives to modulate power down when not necessary.
real_qa.requete: low cost energy waste reduction hospitals

real_qa.q: How does Energy Star Portfolio Manager help healthcare systems benchmark their energy performance?
real_qa.r: Energy Star Portfolio Manager allows facilities to submit data and receive an Energy Star score comparing their performance to benchmarks by building type and climate zone. A score of 50 indicates median performance, 95 places a facility in the top 5%, and 5 indicates bottom 5% performance, helping identify where efficiency improvements are most needed.
real_qa.requete: Energy Star Portfolio Manager healthcare benchmarking

real_qa.q: What are the secondary benefits beyond cost savings for healthcare systems investing in energy efficiency?
real_qa.r: Beyond cost savings, benefits include reducing emissions that counter the health system's mission, gaining PR benefits through demonstrating community stewardship and pollution reduction, engaging local partners, and educating other organizations—since energy efficiency techniques apply across many facility types, not just healthcare.
real_qa.requete: healthcare energy efficiency benefits environmental PR

guest.bio_context: Jeff Rich holds a mechanical engineering degree and worked at John Deere for nearly seven years in Waterloo, Iowa, then spent about 10 years in manufacturing and engineering leadership roles in La Crosse where he became a Lean Six Sigma Master Black Belt. In 2006, he joined Gunderson Health System to lead process improvement efforts, and after achieving 20 percent energy efficiency improvement in 18 months, he led the Envision program which by 2014 offset Gunderson's fossil fuel use with energy efficiency and clean renewables. He retired in 2019 and unretired to launch Eneration in 2024, a spinoff private business helping other health systems with energy waste and clean energy initiatives.
